evidence.use: strong lower-bound evidence that a numerically ample registered-unemployed recruitment pool aged >29 and <=55 exists in every project region. It supports feasibility of recruiting 160 at macro level, not the presence of an AI/digital skill deficit, willingness to participate, full GSCS eligibility, or the 80/40/40 allocation as a need-weight.
limitations: persons aged over 55 are deliberately excluded from the lower-bound calculation to avoid retirement-age ambiguity
other GSCS eligibility/exclusion conditions are not applied to the administrative counts
registered unemployment counts do not measure AI/digital skills or training interest

planned_total_160_vs_age30_55_registered.interpretation: The planned volume is small relative to the conservative age-defined registered-unemployed administrative pool in every region. This is evidence of macro recruitment feasibility only; it cannot be used to infer relative need or to validate the 80/40/40 design as empirically optimal.
